title: benchmarks-matrix-v1 (runtime profile pack) — Jan 2026
content:
Purpose
- This sheet captures the v1 benchmark matrix for validating the Runtime tuning profiles pack.
- Includes: workload buckets, model set, concurrency sweep, raw metrics, and computed deltas vs baseline.
- Used by: Runtime (kernel + scheduler), Applied ML/perf, SRE for perf-canary thresholds.

Important notes / caveats
- These results are from the benchmark-lab harness and should not be treated as customer-facing numbers.
- Absolute performance varies by node (PCIe vs SXM, driver/CUDA, background load). Focus is on deltas and stability.
- TTFT = time to first token (streaming). Queue_ms is time spent queued in scheduler (prefill/decode queue) before compute.

Run metadata (common)
- Harness: benchmark-lab runner (matrix v1)
- Date window: 2026-01-16 to 2026-01-28
- Runtime baselines:
  - Baseline (A): runtime=1.21.7, profile_pack=OFF (legacy defaults)
  - Candidate (B): runtime=1.22.0-rc3, profile_pack=ON, profile_version=1.0.0 (H100/L40S)
- Tokenizer: model-native; measurements at API boundary
- Warmup: 3 min; sample window: 15 min steady-state per cell unless noted
- Request mix: single workload bucket per cell (no mixing) unless explicitly stated

Hardware pools
- H100-SXM (80GB): driver 550.54.14, CUDA 12.4, MIG disabled
- L40S (48GB): driver 550.54.14, CUDA 12.4

Workload buckets (definitions)
- S (short chat): prompt_tokens≈128, output_tokens≈128
- M (medium): prompt_tokens≈512, output_tokens≈256
- LC (long context): prompt_tokens≈4096, output_tokens≈256
- LG (long gen): prompt_tokens≈512, output_tokens≈1024

Model set
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (FP16)
- Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (AWQ int4 where applicable; see Notes column)
- Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (FP16)
- Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (FP16)

Columns (raw)
- sku: H100-SXM-80GB | L40S-48GB
- model
- bucket
- conc: effective client concurrency (requests in-flight)
- req/s
- TTFT_p50_ms / TTFT_p95_ms / TTFT_p99_ms
- Decode_tok_s: median decode throughput per request (tok/s) during decode phase
- Total_tok_s_gpu: aggregate output token throughput per GPU (tok/s)
- Queue_p95_ms: scheduler queue time p95
- Kernel_fallback_%: percent of decode steps using fallback attention kernel path (higher = bad unless expected)
- Peak_mem_GB: max reported alloc during run
- Err_%: non-2xx rate (incl. OOM, timeouts)

Computed deltas (B vs A)
- ΔTTFT_p95: (B - A) / A
- ΔTotal_tok_s_gpu: (B - A) / A
- ΔQueue_p95: (B - A) / A

H100 highlights (quick read)
- Candidate B improved Total_tok_s_gpu by ~7–10% across most cells.
- Kernel_fallback_% dropped materially on 70B + long context, consistent with H100 attention kernel variant v3 selection.
- Queue_p95 improved mostly in S/M buckets (scheduler bucketization). LC improvements are smaller.
- No error rate increase observed in these clean (single-bucket) runs.

L40S highlights (quick read)
- Candidate B improves throughput ~5–7% for most “safe” cells.
- Concurrency sensitivity is high: conc=12 on short chat is clearly above the knee; TTFT + queue time regress (queueing dominates).
- Llama-70B on L40S is not a target workload; even when it runs, tail risk is high. Keep as “allowed but discouraged” and treat errors as expected beyond certain conc.


============================================================
TAB 3 — COMPUTED DELTAS SUMMARY (aggregates)
============================================================

Aggregate summary methodology
- For each sku, compute median ΔTotal_tok_s_gpu across all non-error cells in scope.
- Compute worst-case ΔTTFT_p95 across all cells in scope.
- Mark any cell where B Err_% > 0.5% as “investigate”.

| sku | cells_in_scope | median ΔTotal_tok_s_gpu | worst ΔTTFT_p95 | cells_with_B_Err_%>0.5% | comment |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| H100 | 10 | +8.2% | -4.5% (improved) | 0 | candidate looks clean; proceed to mixed-workload tests |
| L40S | 8 | +5.9% | +10.2% (regressed) | 1 | regression explained by conc=12; tune default caps/guardrails |


============================================================
TAB 4 — NOTES / ANOMALIES / FOLLOW-UPS
============================================================

Anomalies
1) L40S / Llama-8B / S / conc=12: B regressed TTFT and queue time
   - Hypothesis: profile default batching/admission control too permissive for short prompts at high conc; queue grows and dominates.
   - Action: treat conc>8 as overload; enforce profile-aware admission control defaults for L40S.
   - Owners: Lena Fischer (backpressure), Sofia Ivanova (scheduler). Link: github:redwood/pr-24918 (initial cap)

2) L40S / Llama-70B / S / conc=1: B Err_%=2.0
   - One run hit OOM timeout during KV cache growth; rerun was clean.
   - Likely just too close to memory headroom; this workload should be excluded from strict gates on L40S.
   - Action: keep as “informational” cell; add explicit note in expected behavior doc.
   - Owners: Omar El-Sayed / Samir Qureshi.

Follow-ups (for matrix v1.1)
- Add mixed-workload runs (S + M + LC mix) to evaluate tail latency under contention (this is the real risk).
- Add explicit KV cache compaction counters alongside latency for LC buckets.
- Add B200 smoke cells once driver/CUDA baseline stabilizes (see infra memo).
- Add separate embedding-only matrix (batch size sweep, latency SLO at p99).

Open questions
- Should we gate on absolute TTFT_p95 per sku, or only deltas vs baseline? (SRE prefers deltas with hard “blockers” for extreme regressions.)
- For L40S: should the profile pack ship with an explicit concurrency cap, or rely on autoscaler/backpressure? (leaning: ship cap; safer for Dedicated/Private too.)

Appendix: shorthand mapping used in harness
- bucket=S: prompt=128±16, output=128±16
- bucket=M: prompt=512±64, output=256±32
- bucket=LC: prompt=4096±256, output=256±32
- bucket=LG: prompt=512±64, output=1024±64
